$comment: Evidence library the case-conference agents cite. key_point is our paraphrase, not a quote. Entries without a url are well-known references to verify before citing externally.

entries.title: ATLAS: athletic trainer access in US high schools
entries.source: NATA / Korey Stringer Institute (J Athl Train 2019)
entries.key_point: About a third of US high schools have no athletic trainer access; only about 37% of public schools have a full-time trainer.

entries.title: Is the Landing Error Scoring System reliable and valid?
entries.key_point: LESS is a reliable screen of jump-landing errors linked to ACL-injury mechanics; its power to predict injury is still being established.

entries.title: Neuromuscular training and noncontact ACL injuries in female athletes
entries.source: Grindstaff et al., J Athl Train
entries.key_point: Neuromuscular training programs reduced noncontact ACL injuries in female athletes; female athletes in jumping/cutting sports tear ACLs several times more often than males.

entries.title: Preventing ACL injuries in female athletes
entries.key_point: Neuromuscular warm-ups help most when athletes do them consistently; feedback on technique improves the benefit.

entries.title: Change in HRV after concussion in a collegiate soccer player
entries.key_point: Wrist-measured HRV dropped after a concussion and recovered as symptoms resolved, but lagged by about a week, so it tracks recovery and cannot diagnose.

entries.title: Concussion under-reporting in high school athletes
entries.source: Register-Mihalik et al., J Athl Train 2013 (summary)
entries.key_point: Roughly 4 in 10 possible concussions in high school athletes are never reported to a coach or medical professional.

entries.title: The training-injury prevention paradox
entries.key_point: Rapid spikes in training load relative to what an athlete is prepared for (high acute:chronic workload ratio) are associated with higher injury risk; steady, well-built load is protective.

entries.title: Chronic lack of sleep and sports injuries in adolescent athletes
entries.source: Milewski et al., J Pediatr Orthop 2014
entries.key_point: Adolescent athletes who slept less than 8 hours a night had a higher rate of injury than those sleeping 8 or more.

entries.title: Exercise interventions to prevent sports injuries
entries.source: Lauersen et al., Br J Sports Med 2014
entries.key_point: Strength-training programs substantially reduced sports injuries in a meta-analysis of randomized trials.

entries.title: Monitoring training: monotony and strain
entries.key_point: High training monotony (little day-to-day variation) combined with high load (strain) is associated with illness and overtraining.

entries.title: Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs)
entries.source: IOC consensus statement, Br J Sports Med 2023
entries.key_point: Low energy availability (under-fueling relative to training) impairs recovery, bone health and performance and raises injury risk.

entries.title: Consensus statement on concussion in sport (Amsterdam 2022)
entries.key_point: Symptoms can evolve over hours to days after a head impact; any suspected concussion should be removed from play and evaluated by a licensed clinician, who makes return-to-play decisions.
